    A Ghost in Your Ear

    7:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Also on other days Going out

    When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.

    Led by veteran trumpeter Simon Wettenhall and Grammy winning pianist Conal Fowkes, The High Society New Orleans Jazz Band are a New Orleans style Jazz band which for decades have been Woody Allens band of choice for his movies, concert tours and weekly performances.The band have appeared on all the premiere concert stages of Europe and the United States. Band members have appeared in and provided music for Woody Allen movies including: Wild Man Blues, Sweet and Lowdown, Midnight in Paris, Blue Jasmine, Cafe Society, Magic In The Moonlight, and A Rainy Day In New York.Their driving sound is a testament to the ongoing relevance of New Orleans Jazz and they have an international fan base to prove it.     Cyrille Aimée

    7:00 PM · Birdland Jazz Club, Hell's Kitchen · $45.76 Something special

    Cyrille Aime grew up in a multilingual household full of music where dancing was an everyday activity, soundtracked by the Afro-Caribbean sounds of her mothers native Dominican Republic. The family home was in Samois-sur-Seine, the location of the Django Reinhardt Festival, and the teenage Cyrille would climb out of her bendroom window at night to mingle with the players, igniting a passion for jazz. Moving to New York City, her talents quickly gained her a reputation among her peers as a matchless interpreter of song. She performed and recorded with Roy Hargrove and stole the show in front of the notoriously hard-to-please crowd at the Harlem Apollo. Steven Sondheim invited her to star in a tribute at New York Citys City Centre, backed by Wynton Marsalis. Her 2019 album Move On featured versions of Sondheims songs which received praise from Sondheim himself, and her version of Marry Me a Little was nominated for a 2019 GRAMMY award. At the height of her New York success, new horizons beckoned. Visiting New Orleans, she fell in love with the energy and diversity of the city and made it her home. Linking back to New York to connect up all the dots, she teamed up with producer/multi-instrumentalist Jake Sherman, and together they created her latest album, A Fleur de Peau, to be released on a new label, the London-based imprit Whirlwind Records.Combining the depth and sophistication of jazz, the immediacy of pop, the irrepressible dance rhythms of the Caribbean, its more intimate and more accessible than anything Cyrille has done before.

    Ashley Monroe & Charlie Worsham

    9:00 PM · The Bitter End, Greenwich Village · $50.44 Going out

    Ashley Monroe is one of Nashville's most respected and influential voices whose work has helped shape modern country music from the inside out. Over a career spanning nearly 25 years, she's earned GRAMMY nominations, widespread critical acclaim, and the admiration of her peers through both her solo catalog and her work with Pistol Annies. Her recent music marks a bold new chapter of creative clarity and emotional honesty. On her surprise-released album Dear Nashville, written and produced alongside Luke Laird, Monroe turns inward, exploring her complicated relationship with the town that built her. The eight-song concept album captures the tension between deep love for country music and the emotional toll of the industry, delivered with the unfiltered perspective that has long defined her songwriting. With more new music continuing to emerge, Monroe remains as vital as ever---an artist still evolving, still telling the truth, and still finding new ways to be heard. Twenty years after moving to Nashville, Charlie Worsham has established himself as one of Music City's most respected artists: a singer-songwriter, producer, award winning instrumentalist, podcast host, and collaborator. With Once Upon a Second Time Around, he reflects on a life he once dreamed of and realizes he is already living it. Raised in Mississippi on bluegrass, country, and rock & roll, Worsham brings those influences together in a deeply personal album shaped by marriage, fatherhood, friendship, and personal growth. Created after stepping away from the major-label system, the project embraces creative freedom and authenticity over commercial expectations. Rather than chasing trends, Worsham focused on crafting a complete album centered on strong songwriting, musicianship, and honest performances. The songs explore gratitude, resilience, and second chances, ranging from intimate acoustic moments to expansive bluegrass and southern rock arrangements. A two-time ACM Acoustic Guitar Player of the Year and the 2024 CMA Musician of the Year, Worsham delivers his most personal work yet: an album that celebrates growth, perspective, and appreciating what is already in front of him. Please Note: All Sales Final. Two Item Minimum Per Attendee. 18+ admitted if accompanied by parent or guardian.
